Subject: Gated onboarding milestones and renewal uplift refresh

Hi Caroline —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As promised, I attached a focused MAP (Catalyst_MAP_v3.xlsx) that gates the pilot, commercial commit, and the renewal uplift triggers we discussed. High level proposal:

- Week 0–2: Pilot hookup (data access + sandbox model with 10K tokens/day cap)
- Week 3–6: Evaluation ramp (shared eval set, latency & cost baselines, UX pass)
- Week 7–12: Production proof (90-day pilot, usage ramp to 100k tokens/day with rollback policy)
- Post-12 months: Renewal triggers — uplift tied to committed QPS and expansion seats (details in sheet)

Key asks from your side: confirmation of the pilot dataset (PII-scope), preferred success metrics (latency, cost/tok, and quality eval threshold), and procurement timeline so we can align pricing cadence in the MAP.

Pricing notes in the sheet include: a two-step commit ladder — introductory commit with a time-limited credit and a renewal uplift discount schedule that widens with larger year-two commits. If you want, I can convert the MAP into a one-page mutual action checklist for your procurement team.

Attached: Catalyst_MAP_v3.xlsx (MAP + milestone calendar). Also attaching a short security Q&A for your SOC questions (security-QA.pdf).

Proposed next steps:
- Can we lock a 30-min sync next Tue or Wed to finalize the success metrics?
- If procurement prefers, Marissa can run through commercial terms and DocuSign timeline during that call.

Thanks —
Olga Petrov

Caroline —

Thanks for the quick read. Answers inline below and a concise commercial summary at the end.

1) Discount ladder / renewal uplift
- Year 1 (intro ramp): 10% platform credit for any commit >= $60k ARR executed within 60 days of pilot completion.
- Year 2 (renewal uplift): uplifted discount applies if Year 1 actuals meet the commit ladder: 12% base discount + incremental 2–4% volume tiers depending on commit size (sheet shows tiers: $250k+, $500k+, $1M+). Uplift is applied to line items for model serving and support credits.

2) Rollback policy (quality drop)
- If your monitored quality metric (we recommend F1 on the shared eval set + manual spot checks) falls > 10% below the agreed threshold for 2 consecutive weeks, we will:
  - Immediately enable the fallback variant (quantized, lower-cost model) for new requests,
  - Pause auto-scaling for the flagged route, and
  - Initiate a joint remediation sprint (1 week) where we commit engineering hours to stabilize outputs.
- Credits: if remediation doesn't restore agreed performance within 14 days, we will credit service fees pro rata for impacted tokens. Exact SLAs are in the contract language.

3) Pilot cap
- We can start at 20K/day for the evaluation phase. That will give you more representative signal. We'll add a short-term burst clause in the MAP to allow daily spikes up to 35K for up to 5 days.

Commercial summary (short):
- Pilot: 0–3 months — free credits covering up to 20K/day, success metrics and data access confirmed.
- Intro commit: execute within 60 days post-pilot to access 10% intro credit (applies to first-year invoices).
- Renewal uplift: year-two discount band tied to Year 1 actuals and committed ARR; we recommend a mid-year checkpoint (month 9) to review velocity and decide uplift band.

I attached a one-page MAP checklist and redlined SKUs for Marissa to send into procurement. Priyom — added you on the thread to confirm any technical gating (data sync, eval harness) so we can add exact test vectors.

Next steps:
- Confirm Wed Apr 14 10:00 AM PT for the 30-min sync?
- I'll ask Marissa to prepare the commercial summary and a preliminary DocuSign timeline.

Thanks,
Olga
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Thanks — looping in commercial terms and procurement timeline. Quick bullets for your legal/procurement:

- Billing cadence: monthly invoices with a consolidated usage report; upfront invoicing optional for committed ARR bands.
- DocuSign timeline: if we get a signed MSA + SOW within 4 weeks of pilot close, we will honor the intro credit and the stated Year 2 uplift bands.
- Escrow/credits: we can include a 30-day remedy window in the MSA and a token-based credit schedule for outages/remediation.

- Renewal uplift: we like the tiered approach but need a clear hard trigger. Can we tie the Year 2 uplift to a 9-month checkpoint where both parties sign off on velocity? If velocity is met, uplift applies automatically; if not, uplifts are paused until remedied.
- Procurement: we'll aim to have an internal decision by Apr 30. If that's in scope, we're prepared to sign within your 4-week DocuSign timeline.

Assuming audit logs retention is confirmed and we lock the 9-month checkpoint, we are comfortable moving forward. Happy to sign the MSA once the appendix includes the audit-retention clause.
